answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each new agent to lock a refundable stake in a shared vault before it may trade. Like a mesa standing firm while a gale strips loose sand away, the stake makes cheap fake identities costly: an attacker who spawns a thousand clones must fund a thousand deposits, while honest agents earn theirs back by behaving well. Reputation then grows on top of that bonded identity, so volume alone can never buy trust.
